questiontext.text:
Match the coordination compounds with the number of moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitated per mole of the compound on treatment with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) solution in cold:

List I (Compound)List II (Moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitated)
(1) \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 6NH_3}\)(A) \(1\text{ mol}\)
(2) \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 5NH_3}\)(B) \(3\text{ mol}\)
(3) \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 4NH_3}\)(C) \(0\text{ mol}\)
(4) \(\mathrm{PtCl_2 \cdot 2NH_3}\)(D) \(2\text{ mol}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Werner's theory, only the ionisable chloride ions lying outside the coordination sphere (primary valence counter ions) precipitate as \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) when treated with excess cold \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
In \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 6NH_3}\), formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}\), all \(3\) chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere, precipitating \(3\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).
In \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 5NH_3}\), formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2}\), \(2\) chloride ions are ionisable, precipitating \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).
In \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 4NH_3}\), formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]Cl}\), only \(1\) chloride ion is ionisable, precipitating \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).
In \(\mathrm{PtCl_2 \cdot 2NH_3}\), formulated as \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]}\), all \(4\) groups are inside the coordination sphere, so \(0\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) is precipitated.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 6NH_3} \to 3\text{ mol}\), \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 5NH_3} \to 2\text{ mol}\), \(\mathrm{CoCl_3 \cdot 4NH_3} \to 1\text{ mol}\), and \(\mathrm{PtCl_2 \cdot 2NH_3} \to 0\text{ mol}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q02 - Biological and medicinal complexes with central metals

questiontext.text:
Match the biologically or medicinally important coordination compounds with the central metal atom/ion present in them:

List I (Coordination Compound)List II (Central Metal)
(1) Chlorophyll(A) Iron
(2) Haemoglobin(B) Platinum
(3) Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\)(C) Magnesium
(4) cis-Platin(D) Cobalt

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Many vital biological pigments, vitamins, and chemotherapeutic agents are coordination compounds containing specific metal ions at their active centres.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
Chlorophyll, the green pigment responsible for photosynthesis in plants, is a coordination compound of magnesium.
Haemoglobin, the red pigment of blood that acts as an oxygen carrier, is a coordination compound of iron.
Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\) (cyanocobalamin), the anti-pernicious anaemia factor, is a coordination compound of cobalt.
cis-Platin is a coordination compound of platinum used effectively to inhibit the growth of tumours.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: Chlorophyll \(\to\) Magnesium, Haemoglobin \(\to\) Iron, Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\) \(\to\) Cobalt, and cis-Platin \(\to\) Platinum.

questiontext.text:
Match the ligands with their correct classification based on denticity and ligating behaviour:

List I (Ligand)List II (Classification)
(1) \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)(A) Didentate ligand
(2) \(\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}\)(B) Hexadentate ligand
(3) \(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\)(C) Ambidentate ligand
(4) \(\mathrm{SCN^-}\)(D) Unidentate ligand

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ligands are classified by the number of donor atoms they use to bind simultaneously to a central metal ion (denticity), or as ambidentate if they possess two different donor atoms and can ligate through either one.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Ligand
Ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH_3}\)) binds through a single nitrogen donor atom, so it is a unidentate ligand.
Oxalate (\(\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}\)) binds simultaneously through two oxygen donor atoms, making it a didentate ligand.
Ethylenediaminetetraacetate (\(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\)) binds through two nitrogen atoms and four oxygen atoms, making it a hexadentate ligand.
Thiocyanate (\(\mathrm{SCN^-}\)) can coordinate either through the sulphur atom or through the nitrogen atom, so it is an ambidentate ligand.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{NH_3} \to\) Unidentate ligand, \(\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}} \to\) Didentate ligand, \(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}} \to\) Hexadentate ligand, and \(\mathrm{SCN^-} \to\) Ambidentate ligand.

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities with their characteristic coordination polyhedra (geometrical shapes):

List I (Coordination Entity)List II (Geometry)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\)(A) Trigonal bipyramidal
(2) \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\)(B) Octahedral
(3) \(\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}}\)(C) Tetrahedral
(4) \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]}\)(D) Square planar

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The spatial arrangement of ligand donor atoms directly attached to the central metal atom/ion defines the coordination polyhedron.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Complex
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) has coordination number \(6\) and adopts an octahedral geometry.
\(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\) has coordination number \(4\) with \(sp^3\) hybridisation and adopts a tetrahedral geometry.
\(\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}}\) has coordination number \(4\) with \(dsp^2\) hybridisation and adopts a square planar geometry.
\(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]}\) has coordination number \(5\) and adopts a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}} \to\) Octahedral, \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]} \to\) Tetrahedral, \(\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}} \to\) Square planar, and \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]} \to\) Trigonal bipyramidal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q05 - Oxidation numbers of central metal atoms

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination compounds/entities with the oxidation number of their central metal atom:

List I (Complex)List II (Oxidation Number)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}}\)(A) \(+2\)
(2) \(\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\)(B) \(0\)
(3) \(\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)(CN)(en)_2]^{2+}}\)(C) \(+1\)
(4) \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\)(D) \(+3\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The ligand charges are: \(\mathrm{CN^-} = -1\), \(\mathrm{H_2O} = 0\), \(\mathrm{en} = 0\), \(\mathrm{CO} = 0\), and counter ion \(\mathrm{K^+} = +1\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The algebraic sum of the oxidation number of the central metal atom and the charges of all ligands equals the overall charge of the coordination entity.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Let \(x\) represent the oxidation state of the central metal atom in each species.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}}\): \(x + 4(-1) = -3 \implies x = +1\).
For \(\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\): \(4(+1) + x + 6(-1) = 0 \implies x = +2\).
For \(\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)(CN)(en)_2]^{2+}}\): \(x + 0 + (-1) + 2(0) = +2 \implies x = +3\).
For \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\): \(x + 4(0) = 0 \implies x = 0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}} \to +1\), \(\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]} \to +2\), \(\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)(CN)(en)_2]^{2+}} \to +3\), and \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]} \to 0\).

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination compounds with their correct IUPAC systematic names:

List I (Formula)List II (IUPAC Name)
(1) \(\mathrm{K_3[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]}\)(A) Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride
(2) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(CO_3)]Cl}\)(B) Diamminechloridonitrito-N-platinum(II)
(3) \(\mathrm{K_2[Zn(OH)_4]}\)(C) Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II)
(4) \(\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl(NO_2)]}\)(D) Potassium trioxalatochromate(III)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the cation is named first, ligands are listed alphabetically before the metal, anionic ligands end in -o/-ido, and metals in anionic complexes take the suffix -ate followed by the oxidation state in Roman numerals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Formula
\(\mathrm{K_3[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]}\) has potassium counter cations and an anionic chromium(III) complex with three oxalato ligands, giving Potassium trioxalatochromate(III).
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(CO_3)]Cl}\) has a cationic cobalt(III) complex with five ammine and one carbonato ligand, giving Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride.
\(\mathrm{K_2[Zn(OH)_4]}\) has potassium counter cations and an anionic zinc(II) complex with four hydroxido ligands, giving Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II).
\(\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl(NO_2)]}\) is a neutral platinum(II) complex with two ammine, one chlorido, and one N-bonded nitrito ligand, giving Diamminechloridonitrito-N-platinum(II).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{K_3[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]} \to\) Potassium trioxalatochromate(III), \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(CO_3)]Cl} \to\) Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride, \(\mathrm{K_2[Zn(OH)_4]} \to\) Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II), and \(\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl(NO_2)]} \to\) Diamminechloridonitrito-N-platinum(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q07 - Types of structural isomerism in complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the pairs of coordination compounds with the type of structural isomerism they exhibit:

List I (Pair of Complexes)List II (Type of Isomerism)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(ONO)]Cl_2}\)(A) Ionisation isomerism
(2) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]}\)(B) Linkage isomerism
(3) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}\)(C) Solvate isomerism
(4) \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2 \cdot H_2O}\)(D) Coordination isomerism

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Structural isomers differ in the connectivity or bonding of ligands and counter ions within the coordination compound.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(ONO)]Cl_2}\) differ in whether the ambidentate nitrite ligand binds through N or O, illustrating linkage isomerism.
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]}\) arise from interchange of ligands between the cationic and anionic metal entities, illustrating coordination isomerism.
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}\) exchange a coordinated ligand with the counter ion, giving different ions in solution, illustrating ionisation isomerism.
\(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2 \cdot H_2O}\) differ in whether water molecules are directly coordinated or present as lattice solvent, illustrating solvate (hydrate) isomerism.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: the nitrite/nitrito pair \(\to\) Linkage isomerism, the cobalt/chromium salt pair \(\to\) Coordination isomerism, the sulphate/bromide pair \(\to\) Ionisation isomerism, and the aqua/hydrate pair \(\to\) Solvate isomerism.

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities with their stereoisomeric behaviour:

List I (Coordination Entity)List II (Stereoisomeric Characteristic)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}\)(A) Only cis-isomer is optically active
(2) \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}}\)(B) Does not show geometrical isomerism
(3) \(\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}\)(C) Exhibits fac- and mer-geometrical isomers
(4) \(\mathrm{[NiCl_2(PPh_3)_2]}\) (tetrahedral)(D) Exists as dextro and laevo enantiomers

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Stereoisomerism in coordination complexes depends on the coordination number, geometry, and presence of chelate ligands or symmetry elements.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Entity
Octahedral \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}\) of type \(\mathrm{[Ma_3b_3]}\) exhibits facial (fac-) and meridional (mer-) geometrical isomers.
In \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}}\), the trans-isomer is symmetrical, so only the cis-isomer is chiral and optically active.
\(\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}\) is a chiral tris-chelate octahedral complex that exists as a pair of non-superimposable mirror images (dextro and laevo enantiomers).
Tetrahedral complexes such as \(\mathrm{[NiCl_2(PPh_3)_2]}\) do not show geometrical isomerism because all four ligand positions are equivalent relative to one another.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]} \to\) Exhibits fac- and mer-geometrical isomers, \(\mathrm{[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}} \to\) Only cis-isomer is optically active, \(\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}} \to\) Exists as dextro and laevo enantiomers, and tetrahedral \(\mathrm{[NiCl_2(PPh_3)_2]} \to\) Does not show geometrical isomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q09 - Valence bond hybridisation and magnetic behaviour

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions with their hybridisation and magnetic behaviour according to Valence Bond Theory:

List I (Complex Ion)List II (Hybridisation and Magnetic Nature)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\)(A) \(dsp^2\), diamagnetic
(2) \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\)(B) \(d^2sp^3\), diamagnetic
(3) \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\)(C) \(sp^3\), paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons)
(4) \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}\)(D) \(sp^3d^2\), paramagnetic (4 unpaired electrons)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Valence Bond Theory correlates the number of unpaired electrons and ligand field strength with inner or outer orbital hybridisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Complex
In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) (\(3d^6\)) pairs all \(3d\) electrons and undergoes \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation, making it diamagnetic.
In \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}\), \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) (\(3d^6\)) does not pair its \(3d\) electrons and uses outer \(4d\) orbitals for \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation, leaving \(4\) unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).
In \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}\), \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) (\(3d^8\)) pairs all \(3d\) electrons and undergoes \(dsp^2\) hybridisation, making it diamagnetic.
In \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}\), \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) (\(3d^8\)) undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation without pairing, leaving \(2\) unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}} \to d^2sp^3\), diamagnetic; \(\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}} \to sp^3d^2\), paramagnetic (4 unpaired electrons); \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}} \to dsp^2\), diamagnetic; and \(\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}} \to sp^3\), paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q10 - Unpaired electrons in iron and manganese complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the octahedral complex ions with the number of unpaired electrons present in them:

List I (Complex Ion)List II (Number of Unpaired Electrons)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}\)(A) \(5\)
(2) \(\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}\)(B) \(4\)
(3) \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}\)(C) \(1\)
(4) \(\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}\)(D) \(2\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
In \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) and \(\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}\), iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state (\(3d^5\)). In \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) and \(\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}\), manganese is in the \(+3\) oxidation state (\(3d^4\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Strong-field \(\mathrm{CN^-}\) induces spin pairing to form inner orbital \(d^2sp^3\) complexes, whereas weak-field \(\mathrm{F^-}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\) do not pair electrons and form outer orbital \(sp^3d^2\) complexes.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) (\(3d^5\), paired for \(d^2sp^3\)): two pairs and \(1\) unpaired electron remain.
For \(\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}\) (\(3d^5\), unpaired \(sp^3d^2\)): all \(5\) electrons remain unpaired.
For \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}\) (\(3d^4\), paired for \(d^2sp^3\)): one pair and \(2\) unpaired electrons remain.
For \(\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}\) (\(3d^4\), unpaired \(sp^3d^2\)): all \(4\) electrons remain unpaired.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}} \to 1\), \(\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}} \to 5\), \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}} \to 2\), and \(\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}} \to 4\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q11 - Observed colours of transition metal complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities with their observed colours in aqueous solution:

List I (Coordination Entity)List II (Observed Colour)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\)(A) Yellow orange
(2) \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}}\)(B) Blue
(3) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\)(C) Red
(4) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(H_2O)]^{3+}}\)(D) Violet

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The colour of a transition metal complex is complementary to the wavelength of visible light absorbed during \(d\text{--}d\) electronic transitions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Complex
\(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue-green light (\(498\text{ nm}\)) and appears violet.
\(\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}}\) absorbs red light (\(600\text{ nm}\)) and appears blue.
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue light (\(475\text{ nm}\)) and appears yellow orange.
\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(H_2O)]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue-green light (\(500\text{ nm}\)) and appears red.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}} \to\) Violet, \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}} \to\) Blue, \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}} \to\) Yellow orange, and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(H_2O)]^{3+}} \to\) Red.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q12 - Crystal field electronic configurations in octahedral complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the octahedral \(d^n\) metal ion cases with their corresponding crystal field electronic configurations:

List I (Case)List II (Configuration)
(1) \(d^4\) with weak field ligand (\(\Delta_o < P\))(A) \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\)
(2) \(d^4\) with strong field ligand (\(\Delta_o > P\))(B) \(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\)
(3) \(d^6\) with weak field ligand (\(\Delta_o < P\))(C) \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^1\)
(4) \(d^6\) with strong field ligand (\(\Delta_o > P\))(D) \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^2\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In an octahedral crystal field, the first three electrons occupy the \(t_{2g}\) orbitals singly. For \(d^4\) to \(d^7\) configurations, the distribution of subsequent electrons depends on whether \(\Delta_o < P\) (high spin, electrons enter \(e_g\) before pairing) or \(\Delta_o > P\) (low spin, electrons pair in \(t_{2g}\) first).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Working
For \(d^4\) with \(\Delta_o < P\): the fourth electron enters \(e_g\), giving \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^1\).
For \(d^4\) with \(\Delta_o > P\): the fourth electron pairs in \(t_{2g}\), giving \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\).
For \(d^6\) with \(\Delta_o < P\): five electrons occupy \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^2\) singly, and the sixth pairs in \(t_{2g}\), giving \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^2\).
For \(d^6\) with \(\Delta_o > P\): all six electrons pair in the three \(t_{2g}\) orbitals, giving \(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(d^4\) (\(\Delta_o < P\)) \(\to t_{2g}^3 e_g^1\), \(d^4\) (\(\Delta_o > P\)) \(\to t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\), \(d^6\) (\(\Delta_o < P\)) \(\to t_{2g}^4 e_g^2\), and \(d^6\) (\(\Delta_o > P\)) \(\to t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\).

questiontext.text:
Match the homoleptic metal carbonyls with their molecular structures:

List I (Metal Carbonyl)List II (Structure)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]}\)(A) Trigonal bipyramidal
(2) \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]}\)(B) \(\mathrm{Co\text{--}Co}\) bond bridged by two \(\mathrm{CO}\) groups
(3) \(\mathrm{[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]}\)(C) Octahedral
(4) \(\mathrm{[Co_2(CO)_8]}\)(D) Two square pyramidal units joined by \(\mathrm{Mn\text{--}Mn}\) bond

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Homoleptic metal carbonyls adopt well-defined mononuclear or polynuclear geometries depending on the metal's coordination number and metal-metal bonding.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Carbonyl
Hexacarbonylchromium(0), \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]}\), is octahedral.
Pentacarbonyliron(0), \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]}\), is trigonal bipyramidal.
Decacarbonyldimanganese(0), \(\mathrm{[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]}\), consists of two square pyramidal \(\mathrm{Mn(CO)_5}\) units joined by a \(\mathrm{Mn\text{--}Mn}\) bond.
Octacarbonyldicobalt(0), \(\mathrm{[Co_2(CO)_8]}\), has a \(\mathrm{Co\text{--}Co}\) bond bridged by two \(\mathrm{CO}\) groups.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_6]} \to\) Octahedral, \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]} \to\) Trigonal bipyramidal, \(\mathrm{[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]} \to\) Two square pyramidal units joined by \(\mathrm{Mn\text{--}Mn}\) bond, and \(\mathrm{[Co_2(CO)_8]} \to \mathrm{Co\text{--}Co}\) bond bridged by two \(\mathrm{CO}\) groups.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q14 - Industrial and analytical applications of complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the industrial, metallurgical, or analytical processes with the coordination compound or reagent involved:

List I (Process)List II (Complex / Reagent)
(1) Estimation of hardness of water(A) \(\mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-}\)
(2) Extraction of gold(B) \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\)
(3) Purification of nickel(C) \(\mathrm{[Ag(S_2O_3)_2]^{3-}}\)
(4) Fixing developed photographic film(D) \(\mathrm{Na_2EDTA}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Coordination compound formation is widely exploited in volumetric analysis, hydrometallurgy, vapour-phase refining, and photography.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Process
Hardness of water (\(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\)) is estimated by simple titration with \(\mathrm{Na_2EDTA}\).
Gold is extracted by leaching with cyanide in the presence of oxygen and water to form the soluble complex \(\mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-}\).
Impure nickel is purified by converting it into volatile \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\), which is subsequently decomposed to yield pure nickel.
In black-and-white photography, washing the developed film with hypo solution dissolves undecomposed \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) as the soluble complex \(\mathrm{[Ag(S_2O_3)_2]^{3-}}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: Estimation of hardness of water \(\to \mathrm{Na_2EDTA}\), Extraction of gold \(\to \mathrm{[Au(CN)_2]^-}\), Purification of nickel \(\to \mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\), and Fixing developed photographic film \(\to \mathrm{[Ag(S_2O_3)_2]^{3-}}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q15 - Crystal field stabilisation energy of octahedral complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the octahedral coordination entities with their crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE, neglecting pairing energy) in terms of \(\Delta_o\):

List I (Complex Ion)List II (CFSE)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\)(A) \(-0.4\Delta_o\) (high spin \(d^6\))
(2) \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\)(B) \(-0.4\Delta_o\) (\(d^1\))
(3) \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\)(C) \(-2.4\Delta_o\)
(4) \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\)(D) \(-1.2\Delta_o\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Each \(t_{2g}\) electron contributes \(-0.4\Delta_o\) (\(-\frac{2}{5}\Delta_o\)) and each \(e_g\) electron contributes \(+0.6\Delta_o\) (\(+\frac{3}{5}\Delta_o\)) to the CFSE.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Working
In \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}\) is \(d^1\) (\(t_{2g}^1 e_g^0\)): \(\text{CFSE} = 1(-0.4\Delta_o) = -0.4\Delta_o\).
In \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) is \(d^3\) (\(t_{2g}^3 e_g^0\)): \(\text{CFSE} = 3(-0.4\Delta_o) = -1.2\Delta_o\).
In \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\), \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) is high-spin \(d^6\) (\(t_{2g}^4 e_g^2\)): \(\text{CFSE} = 4(-0.4\Delta_o) + 2(+0.6\Delta_o) = -1.6\Delta_o + 1.2\Delta_o = -0.4\Delta_o\).
In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) is low-spin \(d^6\) (\(t_{2g}^6 e_g^0\)): \(\text{CFSE} = 6(-0.4\Delta_o) = -2.4\Delta_o\).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}} \to -0.4\Delta_o\) (\(d^1\)), \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}} \to -1.2\Delta_o\), \(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}} \to -0.4\Delta_o\) (high spin \(d^6\)), and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}} \to -2.4\Delta_o\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q16 - Colour shift in aqueous nickel(II) complexes with ethylenediamine

questiontext.text:
Match the aqueous nickel(II) complexes formed by progressive addition of ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{en}\)) with their observed colours:

List I (Complex)List II (Colour)
(1) \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}(aq)}\)(A) Blue/purple
(2) \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}(aq)}\)(B) Green
(3) \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}(aq)}\)(C) Violet
(4) \(\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}(aq)}\)(D) Pale blue

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Replacing a weaker-field ligand (\(\mathrm{H_2O}\)) progressively with a stronger-field ligand (\(\mathrm{en}\)) increases the crystal field splitting \(\Delta_o\), shifting the absorption to shorter wavelengths and changing the observed colour.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Complex
\(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}(aq)}\) is green in colour.
Upon adding \(\mathrm{en}\) in a \(1:1\) molar ratio, \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}(aq)}\) forms, which is pale blue.
Upon adding \(\mathrm{en}\) in a \(2:1\) molar ratio, \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}(aq)}\) forms, which is blue/purple.
Upon adding \(\mathrm{en}\) in a \(3:1\) molar ratio, \(\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}(aq)}\) forms, which is violet.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct conceptual pairings are: \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}(aq)} \to\) Green, \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}(aq)} \to\) Pale blue, \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}(aq)} \to\) Blue/purple, and \(\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}(aq)} \to\) Violet.
